H1.note: two genes; MUC5B gain-of-function (pos), reduced TOLLIP (neg). The chain's three steps share no node. MUC5B reaches IPF only through bridge B2 (MUC5B injures AT2 cells, from the run's H1.1 citation) and H3's AT2-injury step; TOLLIP has no route.

H2.note: reduced TERT and impaired DSP (both loss-of-function, neg). The chain does not connect: telomere extension and telomere capping are different nodes from 'telomere damage'. DSP reaches IPF through bridge B1 (DSP prevents telomere damage, from the run's own UniProt citation); TERT has no route.

H3.note: SFTPC dysfunction/loss (neg). The chain connects by two routes after the compound split, SFTPC →− AT2 injury →+ IPF and SFTPC →+ AT2 regeneration →− IPF, but every disease-facing step cites only an Open Targets score, so neither arm has kept evidence.

H4.no_claim_reason: the run states the direction of FAM13A's effect is unresolved (step polarity 'unknown', falsification expected 'unknown'); no overall sign to claim

findings.detail: H1.1 ends at ER stress, H1.2 starts at TOLLIP (a new subject) and ends at autophagic clearance, H1.3 starts at 'proteotoxic stress'; no node is shared, so TOLLIP has no route to IPF and MUC5B reaches it only through a bridge from the run's own H1.1 paper (MUC5B injures AT2 cells) and H3's AT2-injury step.

H2.1 ends at telomere extension, H2.2 at desmosome organization and telomere capping ('telomere protection'), H2.3 starts at 'telomere damage and epithelial repair failure'; TERT has no route, and DSP connects only through a bridge from the run's own UniProt citation (DSP 'acts to prevent telomere damage'), a link the mechanism states but no step makes.
H4.1 ends at Rho-dependent signaling, H4.2 starts at 'abnormal epithelial wound-repair signaling'; the nodes are not the same, and both steps are unexpressed anyway.

Every disease-facing step grounds its 'process/phenotype -> IPF' claim on Open Targets gene-disease association scores (OT:MUC5B/TOLLIP/TERT/DSP/SFTPC/FAM13A-EFO_0000768); a gene-disease score states neither the step's subject (a process or phenotype) nor an effect, so all were excluded.

PMID:42120512 (SYISL-DSP-Hippo/YAP driving EMT and fibrosis) was cited for 'telomere damage/repair failure -> IPF' but describes an unrelated DSP-degradation/EMT axis; it does state DSP loss promotes fibrosis, which would fit a DSP->IPF claim the run never made as a step.
PMID:41618408 (Korean IPF cohort) was cited for 'abnormal wound-repair signaling -> IPF' but only reports IPF-associated SNP frequencies and pathway distribution, not a causal step.

Every kept citation sits on a gene-function step (H1.1, H1.2, H2.1, H2.2, H3.1) whose end node is not the next step's subject; every step that reaches IPF (H1.3, H2.3, H3.3, H4.2) has no kept citation, so the gene-to-disease link rests on Open Targets scores.
H1 is rated 'medium' confidence though its chain is disconnected and its only disease-facing evidence is two Open Targets association scores.
H2 is rated 'medium' confidence though its chain is disconnected and its disease-facing evidence is Open Targets scores plus an unrelated EMT paper.

The run's own contradicting citation HPA:ENSG00000164362 shows TERT 'Not detected' and not enriched in lung, undercutting the premise that TERT acts in lung epithelial progenitors; it is an expression record so it cannot refute the causal step, but the hypothesis does not acknowledge it.

Supporting citations Q9HC84 (MUC5B is a gel-forming salivary/cervical mucin, no ER-stress link), HPA:ENSG00000117983 (MUC5B RNA enriched in salivary gland, explicitly NOT lung), and PMID:40887773 (TERT/MUC5B/DSP SNP associations with IPF risk and prognosis) state no chain step; the SNP-association paper could have grounded gene->IPF association statements the run chose not to make.

Several free-text chain nodes are compound ('telomere damage and epithelial repair failure', 'alveolar type II cell injury and failed repair', 'desmosomal epithelial barrier and telomere protection'), forcing compound splits and a BLN term for AT2 injury.
BLN:TelomereDamage for 'telomere damage': GO/HP have telomere maintenance and short-telomere-length terms but no term for the damage event.
BLN:AT2Injury for the 'alveolar type II cell injury' half of 'alveolar type II cell injury and failed repair': HP/MP have AT2 morphology, hyperplasia and number terms but none for injury.

PMID:41091081 states MUC5B->ER stress in one span that fuses spatial transcriptomics of IPF lung (observational) with an in-vitro demonstration ('direct relationship ... in bronchiolar epithelia in vitro'); classified inVitro because the causal 'initiates' rests on the in-vitro work, but a single quoted span can mix two designs.

H3 is rated 'medium' (support 'grounded') though its only disease-facing citation is one Open Targets association score, cited for both H3.2 and H3.3, and its own H3.2 note concedes the evidence does not resolve the mechanism.

PMID:41618408, cited as support at H4.2, reports 'significant depletion of IPF risk variants such as TERT rs2736100 and FAM13A rs2609255' in Korean IPF patients against reference populations, which weakens rather than supports a FAM13A (and TERT) role there; the run does not mention it.
H4.1 cites O94988 ('No curated function statement. Domains: Rho-GAP') and an HPA localisation record; neither states any effect of FAM13A, as the run's own note concedes.

required_for maps to effect pos, but the run's object 'low-tension alveolar surface film' grounds to the quality surface tension (PATO:0001461), which SFTPC lowers; the sign had to be inverted with a sign_note, and the guide has no rule for objects named by a low or high value of a quality.

audit.after: GO:0035966 response to topologically incorrect protein (synonym 'response to misfolded or unfolded protein'); missing_term finding removed
audit.reason: a BLN term is only for when nothing fits; the curator grounded ER stress to the GO response term GO:0034976 (the guide's own example) but rejected the matching response term for proteotoxic stress on the opposite principle ('response, not the state'). The why_no_term itself names GO:0035966.

audit.after: GO:0016233 telomere capping (exact synonym 'telomere end protection')
audit.reason: the run's half-label is 'telomere protection'; GO has it as an exact synonym of telomere capping ('telomeres are protected from degradation and fusion'), while telomere maintenance is length and structure in general. The quote ('acts to prevent telomere damage and maintain telomere length') states both, so it stays.
